supporting_observations.claim: The alerted large outbound transfer is visible at 13:50:50 UTC: Zeek recorded 51,000,389 client-originated bytes, and the proxy recorded 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes in a connection to quickshare-drop.net.
The transfer was made through Chrome running as NWD\ivy.chen; the endpoint network event associates the connection with Chrome process 4120.

Minutes before the transfer, ivy.chen ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip, and Sysmon recorded creation of that archive. This sequence is consistent with preparation for exfiltration, though it does not prove that c.zip was uploaded.

The transfer destination is not among the file-sharing or cloud-storage services approved in the supplied environment context, which makes this large outbound transfer suspicious and supports escalation as suspected data exfiltration.
The observed transfer occurred at 13:50:50 UTC, later than the alert description's approximate 13:46 UTC time, but still within the specified 13:20–14:20 UTC review window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The transfer records identify the destination and client-to-server byte volume, but do not show the uploaded content or filename.
The evidence does not link the c.zip file directly to the quickshare-drop.net transfer.
The supplied records show the connection through the explicit proxy; they do not establish what the remote service did with any uploaded data.
The approximate alert time and the recorded transfer time differ by several minutes.
claims_not_established: That c.zip, or any specific client file, was the content of the transfer.
That ivy.chen knowingly initiated the transfer or had malicious intent.
The identity or reputation of the operator of quickshare-drop.net, or whether the transfer was authorized through an exception not included in the supplied context.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy or service-side records showing the upload request, filename, account, and content or hash, if available.
Endpoint artifacts or forensic collection to determine c.zip's contents, size, and hash and whether Chrome accessed it before the transfer.
Browser history and relevant user or service logs to establish how the upload was initiated and whether it was authorized.
The alert's underlying event timestamp and detection details to reconcile its approximate 13:46 UTC time with the recorded 13:50:50 UTC transfer.
unrelated_findings: A Dropbox updater process ran as SYSTEM on WS-ICHEN-01; Dropbox is not listed among approved software or services in the supplied context. Investigate separately. (T059-00011, T059-00012)

Chrome accessed Google account sign-in pages on WS-ICHEN-01. This is separate from the alerted transfer and should be reviewed under the organization's external-service policy. (T059-00139, T059-00140, T059-00152)
Chrome accessed the AWS console on WS-ICHEN-01. This is separate from the alerted transfer and may warrant a separate review of whether the access was authorized. (T059-00212, T059-00213, T059-00222)
